rules.description: Take profit where the bar's own extreme reaches the entry price plus a multiple of the trade's initial risk: the resting limit order Grimes works at 1R and again at 2R.

complexity.reason: a fixed level computed once at entry and a bar-extreme test

catalog_match.note: the same level close-based and stated in dollars is TakeProfit at takeProfit = riskMultiple x stopDistance x BigPointValue; this fires on the BAR'S OWN EXTREME, which is the limit fill Grimes describes, and carries no stop leg (StopLossTakeProfitDollar ORs one in off the same risk unit). Author only if the intrabar fill is wanted

rules.merge_notes: Six restatements of one target: 1R on failure tests (G06-10), failed breakouts (G06-59) and as standing discipline (G08-05, G10-01), 2R for the second tranche (G08-06), and G06-19 spanning both. Book values 1 and 2 - a grid range, not two rules. The partial fractions (25-50 percent, 'more than half') are position sizing the pane system cannot express; recorded, not mechanized.

rules.description: The measured move objective: the coming leg is projected to equal the previous one, D = C + multiple x (B - A) over the last three confirmed pivots.
rules.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && haveTarget && high[0] >= pivotC + multiple * (pivotB - pivotA) - toleranceTicks * ctx.MinMove()

complexity.reason: three confirmed pivots located by a scan

catalog_match.note: identical projection over identical pivot occurrences; the catalog rule already carries the multiple and the tolerance

rules.merge_notes: Five statements of the MMO - the trend's follow-through leg (G03-18), the shared primitive (G06-02), the complex pullback's second leg (G06-30), the Anti's first thrust (G06-38) and the failure-pullback sequence (G05-20). All are D = C +/- (B - A); only the pattern naming the pivots differs. Grimes calls it a zone, not a level, which is the tolerance input.

rules.description: The height of the consolidation or base that preceded the breakout, projected forward from the broken extreme.

complexity.reason: two window extremes captured at entry

catalog_match.note: the catalog rule captures Highest(High[1], refBars) and Lowest(Low[1], refBars) at entry and projects anchor + multiple x height, which is this exactly

rules.merge_notes: The breakout-base target (G06-50) and the glossary definition (G16-24) are one rule, and the window form needs no pivot detection. Grimes warns that prebreakout volatility contraction makes base-width targets too conservative - that is a grid note (let multiple run above 1), not a second rule.

rules.description: The first, most conservative target for a pullback trade: the pivot extreme of the setup leg, the swing high the pullback fell away from.
rules.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && haveTargetHi && high[0] >= swingHigh(pivotIndex, swingStrength) - toleranceAtr * atr(atrLength)

complexity.reason: swing-pivot detection with the no-pivot-found guard

catalog_match.note: the catalog rule at pivotIndex 1 is this target; its `toleranceAtr` also takes the target that many ATRs SHORT of the pivot, which is Grimes's 'place the limit inside the visible chart point'; ExitAtPriorRangeExtreme is the same idea with a rolling window in place of the pivot scan

rules.merge_notes: RECONCILED: swing_structure's identical row is folded in here, bringing G08-24 — take profit a little INSIDE the visible pivot, which is this rule at toleranceAtr about 0.25 rather than 0, a grid value and nothing to author (his tick spelling is expressible since ctx.MinMove()/ctx.PriceScale() were registered, but the ATR spelling is the corpus convention). 'The pivot high of the setup leg is an ideal target and should be considered the first, most conservative profit target for any pullback trade.' G06-18's window restatement is rejected: a Highest window containing bar 0 (or growing with BarsSinceEntry) makes the target trivially reachable. The frozen-window reading is ExitAtPriorRangeExtreme, also already in the catalog.

rules.description: Take profit where the bar's extreme reaches the parallel channel line projected on the far side of the trend.
rules.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && haveLine && high[0] >= channelLineValue(0) - touchTolAtr * atr(atrLength)

complexity.reason: a two-pivot line projected forward to the current bar

catalog_match.note: same line construction from the two most recent same-side pivots, same bar-extreme test

rules.merge_notes: 'If you are long in an uptrend and prices rise to the upper parallel trend line, it probably makes sense to be slightly defensive and take some profits.' Same target as the catalog rule; the partial sizing is out of scope, as it is for every target here.

rules.description: The bar's range is an extreme outlier against recent volatility and the position is in profit: take the windfall on that bar instead of assuming the move continues.
rules.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && (high[0] - low[0]) >= extremeRangeMultiple * atr(atrLength) && close[0] > ctx.EntryPrice()

complexity.reason: one bar's range against an ATR plus a profit gate

catalog_match.note: that rule also requires a with-trend BODY (body >= bodyFraction x range) and a prior run of at least minTrendBars trend bars; this one requires only an outlier range while in profit, so an enormous bar that closes against its own open still fires it

rules.merge_notes: 'On those very rare occasions when the market offers windfall profits, take them' (Grimes's example is the 2010 Flash Crash). Range against ATR is a pure difference, so it passes the shift test. 4x ATR is the miner's guess, not a number Grimes gives; ConsecutiveTrendBarsClimaxExit is the nearest cousin on the in-profit gate.

dropped.reason: composition of ProfitTargetAtRiskMultiple + SwingPivotTarget: the candidate takes min() of the two target levels, and because exits are ORed, placing both rules already exits at whichever level price reaches first, which is that same min()
composition of ProfitTargetAtRiskMultiple + SwingPivotTarget, as G08-25 - the 1R target capped at the nearest visible swing level is the OR of the two rules

sent to context_regime and adjudicated there in the reconciliation pass: dropped as a composition of MovingAverageSlopeTrendFilter at the 5x higher-timeframe lengths (decision 15) + a measured-move target on that series not yet reached (decision 26)
not mechanizable: a position-sizing rule on a pyramided add-on (exit more than was added when the add-on fails). No bar-level condition, and the engine carries no per-tranche position state

cross_bucket.note: a scratch on an early opposite strong bar, not a target; merged there as ScratchExitOnEarlyOppositeStrongBar
a confirmation-counted stop below the base's support, not a target; merged there as StopAfterConsecutiveClosesBeyondLevel
a time-and-flatness scratch exit; merged there as FlatTradeScratchExit

options: model each risk-multiple tranche as a FULL exit placement and let the grid choose one level
add fractional-exit support to the engine
drop the fractions and keep only the first target
design_decisions.recommended: model each tranche as a full exit placement: every exit in the corpus closes the whole position, and Grimes's 25-50 percent at 1R / down to a third by 2R is sizing, not a bar condition. Record the fractions in the rule notes only

bucket_summary: 24 candidates collapsed to 6 rules, 4 drops and 3 strays (the reconciliation pass dropped the G07-27 send and folded swing_structure's SwingPivotTarget row into this bucket's row of that key). The bucket is dominated by two things Brooks already gave the catalog: the measured move objective (five restatements, all LegOneEqualsLegTwoTarget) and structural targets at a prior swing pivot or a channel line. Four of the six rules are therefore duplicates, and the collapse ratio is the finding: Grimes adds no target mechanism the corpus lacks. The A-list is ProfitTargetAtRiskMultiple - six restatements of one rule at 1R and 2R, the book's single most repeated exit - and WindfallRangeExpansionExit, the outlier-bar exit. 'Target capped at the nearest swing level' (G08-25, G10-02) is dropped because ORed exits already fire at whichever of the two levels comes first, which is the min() those candidates compute. RISK MULTIPLES: the engine has no initial-risk accessor, so every NR level here is expressed with a stopDistance parameter in points, which the placement must be set to match the stop rule it is paired with - said once here rather than on each rule.
